e: And these are the descendants of Yitzchok son of Avraham.
Avraham was the father of Yitzchok.

t: כַּד נְסֵיב יָת רִבְקָה בַּת בְּתוּאֵל אֲרַמָּאָה
e: Yitzchok was forty years old
when he took Rivkah, the daughter of Besueil, the Aramite,
of Padan Aram,
sister of Lavan, the Aramite, for a wife.
Yitzchok prayed to [before] Adonoy across from [opposite] his wife,
for she was barren.
Adonoy granted his prayer
and his wife, Rivkah, conceived.
The children clashed [pressed] inside her,
and [when this happened] she said, If this is so,
why did I desire this?
She [then] went to inquire of [to ask for instruction from before] Adonoy.

h: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה לָ֗הּ שְׁנֵ֤י גיים [גוֹיִם֙] בְּבִטְנֵ֔ךְ
t: וַאֲמַר יְיָ לַהּ תְּרֵין עַמְמִין בִּמְעַיְכִי
e: Adonoy said to her, Two nations are in your womb,
and two Kingdoms will separate from within you.
One government will be mightier than the other,
but the greater one will serve the smaller one.
When her days of pregnancy were completed,
behold, there were twins in her womb.
The first one came out with a reddish complexion,
covered completely with what was like a hairy robe,
and they named him Eisov.

h: וְאַֽחֲרֵי־כֵ֞ן יָצָ֣א אָחִ֗יו וְיָד֤וֹ אֹחֶ֙זֶת֙ בַּעֲקֵ֣ב עֵשָׂ֔ו
t: וּבָתַר כֵּן נְפַק אֲחוּהִי וִידֵיהּ אֲחִידָא בְּעִקְבָא דְעֵשָׂו
וְיִצְחָק בַּר שִׁתִּין שְׁנִין כַּד יְלִידַת יָתְהוֹן:
e: After that his brother came out, his hand grasping the heel of Eisov,
and he [Yitzchok] named him Yaakov.
Yitzchok was sixty years old when she [Rivkah] gave birth to them.

h: וַיְהִ֣י עֵשָׂ֗ו אִ֛ישׁ יֹדֵ֥עַ צַ֖יִד אִ֣ישׁ שָׂדֶ֑ה
t: וַהֲוָה עֵשָׂו גְּבַר נַחְשִׁירְכָן גְּבַר נָפֵק לְחַקְלָא
e: The lads grew up.
Eisov became a skilled trapper [an idle man], a man of the field [a man going out to the field].
Yaakov was a wholesome man,
living in tents [serving in the house of study].

t: וּרְחֵם יִצְחָק יָת עֵשָׂו אֲרֵי מִצֵּידֵיהּ הֲוָה אָכִיל
e: Yitzchok loved Eisov because he ate of his trappings,
but Rivkah loved Yaakov.

t: וַאֲתָא (<small>נ"א </small> וְעַל) עֵשָׂו מִן חַקְלָא וְהוּא מְשַׁלְּהֵי:
e: Yaakov was simmering a pottage
when Eisov came in from the field, exhausted.

h: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר עֵשָׂ֜ו אֶֽל־יַעֲקֹ֗ב הַלְעִיטֵ֤נִי נָא֙ מִן־הָאָדֹ֤ם הָאָדֹם֙ הַזֶּ֔ה
t: וַאֲמַר עֵשָׂו לְיַעֲקֹב אַטְעֵמְנִי כְעַן מִן סִמּוֹקָא סִמּוֹקָא הָדֵין
e: Eisov said to Yaakov, Please [Now] give me a swallow of this red [pottage],
for I am exhausted.
He was therefore named Edom [Red].
Yaakov said,
As of this day [Like this day], sell your birthright to me.
Eisov said,
Here I am going to die,
what [good] is this birthright to me.

t: וַאֲמַר יַעֲקֹב קַיֵּם לִי כְּיוֹם דִּלְהֵן
e: Yaakov said, Swear to me as of this day [like this day].
He swore to him,
and sold his birthright to Yaakov.

h: וְיַעֲקֹ֞ב נָתַ֣ן לְעֵשָׂ֗ו לֶ֚חֶם וּנְזִ֣יד עֲדָשִׁ֔ים
t: וְיַעֲקֹב יְהַב לְעֵשָׂו לְחֵם וְתַבְשִׁיל דִּטְלוֹפְחִין
e: Yaakov then gave Eisov bread and a pottage of lentils.
He [Eisov] ate and drank,
got up and left.
[Thus] Eisov scorned the birthright.

t: וַאֲזַל יִצְחָק לְוַת אֲבִימֶלֶךְ מַלְכָּא דִפְלִשְׁתָּאֵי לִגְרָר:
e: There was a famine in the land,
aside from the first famine
that was in the days of Avraham.
Yitzchok went to Avimelech, king of the Philistines, in Gerar.
Adonoy appeared [became revealed] to him
and said, Do not go down to Egypt.
Settle in the land
that I will make known to you.

t: אֲרֵי לָךְ וְלִבְנָךְ אֶתֵּן יָת כָּל אַרְעָתָא הָאִלֵּין
e: Stay temporarily in this land
and I will be with you and bless you [My Word will be your support and I will bless you],
for to you and your descendants I will give all these lands.
I will [thus] keep the oath
that I swore to Avraham, your father.

t: וְאַסְגֵּי יָת בְּנָךְ סַגִּיאִין כְּכוֹכְבֵי שְׁמַיָּא
e: I will make your descendants [as numerous] as the stars of the heavens,
and I will give your descendants
all these lands.
Through [Because of] your descendants shall be blessed
all the nations of the world.
[All this is] because Avraham listened to [accepted] My voice [Word],
and minded My mandate [the mandate of My Word],
My commandments, My decrees and My teachings.
Yitzchok [thus] settled in Gerar.

t: וּשְׁאִילוּ אֲנָשֵׁי אַתְרָא (<small>ס"א</small> עַל עֵיסַק אִתְּתֵיהּ) לְאִתְּתֵיהּ
דִּלְמָא יִקְטְלֻנַּנִי אֲנָשֵׁי אַתְרָא עַל רִבְקָה
e: The local men asked about his wife,
and he said, She is my sister.
He was afraid to say, [she is] my wife,
lest the local men kill me for Rivkah,
for she is so good looking.

t: וַהֲוָה כַּד סְגִיאוּ לֵיהּ תַּמָּן יוֹמַיָּא
e: Once, after [Yitzchok] had been there a long while,
Avimelech, king of the Philistines, looked
at the window,
and he saw, and behold, Yitzchok was amusing himself
with Rivkah, his wife.

h: וַיִּקְרָ֨א אֲבִימֶ֜לֶךְ לְיִצְחָ֗ק וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ אַ֣ךְ הִנֵּ֤ה אִשְׁתְּךָ֙ הִ֔וא
t: וּקְרָא אֲבִימֶלֶךְ לְיִצְחָק וַאֲמַר בְּרַם הָא אִתְּתָךְ הִיא
e: Avimelech called Yitzchok and he said, But she is your wife.
How could you have said, She is my sister?
Yitzchok said to him,
Because I said,
I might die because of her.

t: כִּזְעֵר פּוֹן שָׁכִיב דִּמְיָחֵד בְּעַמָּא עִם אִתְּתָךְ
e: Avimelech said,
What have you done to us?
One of the people [The unique one among the people] could have easily slept with your wife,
and you would have brought guilt upon us.

h: הַנֹּגֵ֜עַ בָּאִ֥ישׁ הַזֶּ֛ה וּבְאִשְׁתּ֖וֹ מ֥וֹת יוּמָֽת׃
e: Avimelech [then] commanded
all his people, saying,
Whoever touches [injures] this man or his wife, shall die.

t: וְאַשְׁכַּח בְּשַׁתָּא הַהִיא עַל חַד מְאָה בִדְשַׁעֲרוֹהִי
e: Yitzchok planted in that land,
and in that year he reaped a hundred fold [more than that which they estimated],
for Adonoy had blessed him.
The man prospered.
He continued to prosper
[and increase] until he became very great.

t: וַהֲוָה לֵיהּ גֵּיתֵי עָנָא וְגֵיתֵי תוֹרִין
e: He owned flocks of sheep, herds of cattle,
and many slaves,
and the Philistines were jealous of him.

t: וְכָל בֵּירִין דִּי חֲפָרוּ עַבְדֵי אֲבוּהִי
e: All the wells that his father’s servants had dug
in the days of his father, Avraham —
the Philistines plugged them,
and filled them with earth.
Avimelech said to Yitzchok,
Go away from us.
You have become much more powerful than us.
Yitzchok went away from there.
He camped in the valley of Gerar and settled there.

h: וַיָּ֨שָׁב יִצְחָ֜ק וַיַּחְפֹּ֣ר אֶת־בְּאֵרֹ֣ת הַמַּ֗יִם אֲשֶׁ֤ר חָֽפְרוּ֙ בִּימֵי֙ אַבְרָהָ֣ם אָבִ֔יו
וַיִּקְרָ֤א לָהֶן֙ שֵׁמ֔וֹת כַּשֵּׁמֹ֕ת אֲשֶׁר־קָרָ֥א לָהֶ֖ן אָבִֽיו׃
t: וְתָב יִצְחָק וְחָפַר יָת בֵּירֵי דְמַיָּא דִּי חֲפָרוּ בְּיוֹמֵי אַבְרָהָם אֲבוּהִי
וּקְרָא לְהֵן שְׁמָהָן כִּשְׁמָהָן דִּי הֲוָה קָרֵי לְהֵן אֲבוּהִי:
e: Yitzchok returned and excavated the wells of water which were dug in the days of his father, Avraham,
and were plugged by the Philistines
after Avraham’s death.
He gave them the same names that his father had given them.
Yitzchok’s servants dug in the valley
and found there a well of spring [flowing] water.

h: וַיָּרִ֜יבוּ רֹעֵ֣י גְרָ֗ר עִם־רֹעֵ֥י יִצְחָ֛ק לֵאמֹ֖ר לָ֣נוּ הַמָּ֑יִם
t: וּנְצוֹ רַעֲוָתָא דִגְרָר עִם רַעֲוָתָא דְיִצְחָק לְמֵימַר דִּי לָנָא מַיָּא
e: The shepherds of Gerar argued with the shepherds of Yitzchok, saying, the water is ours.
He named the well Eisek [Quarrel],
because they had quarreled with him.
They dug another well
and they also argued about it.
He named the well Sitnah [Obstruction].

h: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר כִּֽי־עַתָּ֞ה הִרְחִ֧יב יְהוָ֛ה לָ֖נוּ וּפָרִ֥ינוּ בָאָֽרֶץ׃
t: וַאֲמַר אֲרֵי כְעַן אַפְתֵּי יְיָ לָנָא וְנִיפּוּשׁ (<small>נ"א</small> וְיַפְשִׁנָּנָא) בְּאַרְעָא:
e: He moved away from there and he dug another well,
and there was no argument over it.
He named it Rechovos [Wide Spaces],
and said, For now Adonoy has made room for us, and we shall be fruitful in the land.
From there he went to Beer Sheva.
Adonoy appeared [became revealed] to him that night
and said, I am the God of your father, Avraham.
Do not fear for I am with you [My Word is your support].
I will bless you and make your descendants numerous,
because of My servant, Avraham.

h: וַיִּ֧בֶן שָׁ֣ם מִזְבֵּ֗חַ וַיִּקְרָא֙ בְּשֵׁ֣ם יְהוָ֔ה
e: He [Yitzchok] built an altar there, and proclaimed [prayed in] the Name of Adonoy.
He set up his tent there,
and Yitzchok’s servants dug a well there.
Avimelech came to Yitzchok from Gerar
along with a group of friends
and Pichol, his general.
Yitzchok said to them,
Why have you come to me?
You hate me
and drove me away from you.

h: וַיֹּאמְר֗וּ רָא֣וֹ רָאִינוּ֮ כִּֽי־הָיָ֣ה יְהוָ֣ה עִמָּךְ֒
וַנֹּ֗אמֶר תְּהִ֨י נָ֥א אָלָ֛ה בֵּינוֹתֵ֖ינוּ בֵּינֵ֣ינוּ וּבֵינֶ֑ךָ
t: וַאֲמָרוּ מֶחֱזָא חֲזֵינָא אֲרֵי הֲוָה מֵימְרָא דַיְיָ בְּסַעְדָּךְ
וַאֲמַרְנָא תִּתְקַיַּם כְּעַן מוֹמָתָא דִּהֲוָה בֵין אֲבָהָתָנָא בֵּינָנָא וּבֵינָךְ
e: They said, We have indeed seen that Adonoy is with you [the Word of Adonoy is your support],
and we said, Let there now be an oath between us, [Let the oath that was between our fathers now be established] between ourselves and you,
and let us make a covenant with you;

h: אִם־תַּעֲשֵׂ֨ה עִמָּ֜נוּ רָעָ֗ה כַּאֲשֶׁר֙ לֹ֣א נְגַֽעֲנ֔וּךָ
t: אִם תַּעְבֵּד עִמָּנָא בִּישָׁא כְּמָא דִּי לָא אַנְזִיקְנָךְ
וּכְמָא דִי עֲבַדְנָא עִמָּךְ לְחוֹד טַב
e: that you will do us no harm, just as we did not touch [injure] you.
We did nothing but good to you,
and sent you away in peace.
You are now the blessed one of Adonoy.
He [Yitzchok] made a feast for them,
and they ate and drank.
They got up early in the morning,
and they each swore to the other.
Yitzchok sent them away
and they left in peace.

h: וַיְהִ֣י בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא וַיָּבֹ֙אוּ֙ עַבְדֵ֣י יִצְחָ֔ק
t: וַהֲוָה בְּיוֹמָא הַהוּא וַאֲתוֹ עַבְדֵי יִצְחָק
e: On that day Yitzchok’s servants came
and told him
about the well they had dug;
and they said to him, We have found water.

t: עַל כֵּן שְׁמָא דְקַרְתָּא בֵּארָא דְשֶׁבַע (<small>נ"א</small> בְּאֵר שֶׁבַע)
e: He named it Shiva.
Therefore the city is called Beer Sheva
until this very day.
Eisov was forty years old
and he married Yehudis,
the daughter of Be’eri, the Chittite
and Bosmas, the daughter of Eylon the Chittite.
They were rebellious of spirit to [They were rebels and aggravators against the words of]
Yitzchok and Rivkah.

h: וַיִּקְרָ֞א אֶת־עֵשָׂ֣ו בְּנ֣וֹ הַגָּדֹ֗ל וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֵלָיו֙ בְּנִ֔י
t: וּקְרָא יָת עֵשָׂו בְּרֵיהּ רַבָּא וַאֲמַר לֵיהּ בְּרִי
e: And when Yitzchok grew old
his eyesight faded and he could not see.
He called Eisov, his elder son, and said to him, My son.
[Eisov] said to him, Here I am.
[Yitzchok] said, Behold, if you please [now], I am old.
I do not know the day of my death.
Now [therefore] please [now] take your equipment,
your sword and your bow,
and go out to the field
and trap [deer] for me.

h: וַעֲשֵׂה־לִ֨י מַטְעַמִּ֜ים כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר אָהַ֛בְתִּי וְהָבִ֥יאָה לִּ֖י וְאֹכֵ֑לָה
t: וְעִבֵיד לִי תַבְשִׁילִין כְּמָא דְרְחֵימִית וְאָעֵל לִי וְאֵיכוּל
בְּדִיל דִּי תְבָרֵכִנָּךְ נַפְשִׁי עַד לָא אֵימוּת:
e: Make it into a tasty dish for me, the way I like it, and bring it to me that I may eat,
so that my soul will bless you before I die.
Rivkah had [over]heard
what Yitzchok said
to his son, Eisov.
Eisov went out to the field
to trap [deer] to bring it [home.]

t: וְרִבְקָה אֲמָרַת לְוַת יַעֲקֹב בְּרַהּ לְמֵימָר
e: Rivkah said to her son Yaakov, saying,
Behold, I heard your father
speaking to your brother Eisov, saying,

h: הָבִ֨יאָה לִּ֥י צַ֛יִד וַעֲשֵׂה־לִ֥י מַטְעַמִּ֖ים וְאֹכֵ֑לָה
t: אֱתִי לִי צֵידָא וְעִבֵיד לִי תַבְשִׁילִין וְאֵיכוּל
e: Bring back [deer] for me and make it into a tasty dish for me and I will eat.
I will then bless you in the presence of Adonoy before I die.
Now my son, listen to [accept] me,
concerning that which I command you.

h: וְקַֽח־לִ֣י מִשָּׁ֗ם שְׁנֵ֛י גְּדָיֵ֥י עִזִּ֖ים טֹבִ֑ים
וְאֶֽעֱשֶׂ֨ה אֹתָ֧ם מַטְעַמִּ֛ים לְאָבִ֖יךָ כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר אָהֵֽב׃
t: וְסַב לִי מִתַּמָּן תְּרֵין גַּדְיֵי (בַר) עִזִּין טָבָן
וְאֶעְבֵּד יָתְהוֹן תַּבְשִׁילִין לְאָבוּךְ כְּמָא דִי רְחֵם:
e: Go, please [now], to the sheep
and take for me from there two choice young goats,
and I will make [from] them a tasty dish for your father as he likes.
You will [then] bring it to your father to eat,
in order that he will bless you before he dies.
Yaakov said to Rivkah, his mother,
Behold, Eisov, my brother is a hairy person
and I am a smooth-skinned person.

t: וְאֵהֵי מַיְתֵי (נ"א וָאֱהִי מַיְתֵי) עֲלַי לְוָטִין וְלָא בִרְכָן:
e: Suppose my father touches me.
I will be in his eyes as an impostor [a mocker].
I will bring upon myself a curse [curses]—not a blessing [blessings].

t: עֲלַי אִתְאַמַּר בִּנְבוּאָה דְּלָא יֵיתוּן לְוָטַיָּא עֲלָךְ בְּרִי
e: His mother said to him,
Your curse shall be upon me [It was said regarding me in a prophecy that curses will not come upon you], my son;
but listen to [accept] me. Go bring them to me.
He went, took [them],
and brought [them] to his mother.
His mother make a tasty dish
as his father liked.

h: וַתִּקַּ֣ח רִ֠בְקָה אֶת־בִּגְדֵ֨י עֵשָׂ֜ו בְּנָ֤הּ הַגָּדֹל֙ הַחֲמֻדֹ֔ת
t: וּנְסִיבַת רִבְקָה יָת לְבוּשֵׁי עֵשָׂו בְּרַהּ רַבָּא דָּכְיָתָא
e: Rivkah took the garments of Eisov, her elder son, [the garments] that were precious [to him] [the clean ones]
that were in her keeping in the house,
and put them on Yaakov, her younger son.
The skins of the young goats
she placed on his hands
and the smooth part of his neck.

t: וִיהָבַת יָת תַּבְשִׁילַיָּא וְיָת לַחֲמָא דִּי עֲבָדַת
e: She placed the tasty dish and the bread which she had made,
in the hand of Yaakov, her son.
He came to his father and said, My father.
[Yitzchok] said, Here I am.
Who are you my son?

h: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יַעֲקֹ֜ב אֶל־אָבִ֗יו אָנֹכִי֙ עֵשָׂ֣ו בְּכֹרֶ֔ךָ
t: וַאֲמַר יַעֲקֹב לַאֲבוּהִי אֲנָא עֵשָׂו בּוּכְרָךְ
עֲבָדִית כְּמָא דִי מַלֵּילְתָּא עִמִּי (<small>נ"א</small> לִי)
e: Yaakov said to his father, It is I, Eisov your firstborn.
I have done as you told me.
Rise, if you please [now], sit up [recline] and eat of my trapping
so that your soul will bless me.

h: וַיֹּ֕אמֶר כִּ֥י הִקְרָ֛ה יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ לְפָנָֽי׃
t: וַאֲמַר אֲרֵי זַמִּין יְיָ אֱלָהָךְ קֳדָמָי:
e: Yitzchok said to his son,
How is it that you found it so quickly my son?
He [Yaakov] said, Because Adonoy, your God, brought it about for me.

t: הַאַתְּ דֵּין בְּרִי עֵשָׂו אִם לָא:
e: Yitzchok said to Yaakov,
Come close, if you please [now], and let me touch you, my son.
Are you my son Eisov or not?

t: וּקְרֵיב יַעֲקֹב לְוַת יִצְחָק אֲבוּהִי וּמָשְׁיֵהּ
e: Yaakov came close to Yitzchok, his father, and he [Yitzchok] touched him.
He said, The voice is the voice of Yaakov,
but the hands are the hands of Eisov.

h: כִּֽי־הָי֣וּ יָדָ֗יו כִּידֵ֛י עֵשָׂ֥ו אָחִ֖יו שְׂעִרֹ֑ת
t: אֲרֵי הֲוָאָה יְדוֹהִי כִּידֵי עֵשָׂו אֲחוּהִי שְׂעִירָן (<small>נ"א</small> שַׂעֲרַנְיָן)
e: He [Yitzchok] did not recognize him
because his hands were like those of Eisov, his brother — they were hairy —
and [thus] he blessed him.
He said, Are you indeed my son, Eisov?
[Yaakov] said, [Behold] I am.

h: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר הַגִּ֤שָׁה לִּי֙ וְאֹֽכְלָה֙ מִצֵּ֣יד בְּנִ֔י
e: He said, Bring it close to [before] me and I will eat from my son’s trappings,
so that my soul will bless you.
He brought it close to him and he ate.
He [then] brought him wine and he drank.

t: קְרֵיב כְּעַן וּנְשַׁק לִי (נ"א וְשַׁק לִי) בְּרִי:
e: His father Yitzchok said to him,
Come close to me [now] and kiss me, my son.
He came close and kissed him.
He [Yitzchok] smelled the fragrance of his garments, and he blessed him.
He said, See, my son’s fragrance
is like the fragrance of a field
blessed by Adonoy.
And may God give you
of the dew of heaven,
and of the fatness [riches] [goodness] of the land,
and abundance of grain and wine.
Peoples will serve you and nations bow to you [kingdoms will be subservient to you].
Be master over your brothers,
and your mother’s sons will bow to you.
Those who curse you are [will be] cursed,
and those who bless you are [will be] blessed.

h: וַיְהִ֗י כַּאֲשֶׁ֨ר כִּלָּ֣ה יִצְחָק֮ לְבָרֵ֣ךְ אֶֽת־יַעֲקֹב֒
t: וַהֲוָה כַּד שֵׁיצִי יִצְחָק לְבָרָכָא יָת יַעֲקֹב
e: It was when Yitzchok had finished blessing Yaakov,
and Yaakov had just left
the presence of Yitzchok, his father,
that Eisov came back from his trapping.

h: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לְאָבִ֗יו יָקֻ֤ם אָבִי֙ וְיֹאכַל֙ מִצֵּ֣יד בְּנ֔וֹ
t: וַאֲמַר לַאֲבוּהִי יָקוּם אַבָּא וְיֵכוּל מִצֵּידָא דִבְרֵיהּ
e: He too made a tasty dish
and brought it to his father.
He said to his father, Let my father rise and eat of his son’s trapping,
that your soul may bless me.

t: וַאֲמַר לֵיהּ יִצְחָק אֲבוּהִי מָן אָתְּ
e: Yitzchok, his father, said to him, Who are you?
He said, I am your son, your firstborn, Eisov.

h: וַיֹּ֡אמֶר מִֽי־אֵפ֡וֹא ה֣וּא הַצָּֽד־צַיִד֩ וַיָּ֨בֵא לִ֜י וָאֹכַ֥ל מִכֹּ֛ל בְּטֶ֥רֶם תָּב֖וֹא וָאֲבָרֲכֵ֑הוּ
t: וַאֲמַר מָן הוּא דֵיכִי דְּצָד צֵידָא וְאָעֵיל לִי וַאֲכָלִית מִכֹּלָּא עַד לָא תֵיעוֹל וּבָרֵכִתֵּיהּ
e: Yitzchok was seized with a powerful trembling [Yitzchok was astonished with great astonishment];
and said, Who, then, is he who trapped [deer] and brought it to me. I ate all of it before you came, and I blessed him.
He shall be blessed.

t: כַּד שְׁמַע עֵשָׂו יָת פִּתְגָּמֵי אֲבוּהִי
וּצְוַח צִוְחָא רַבָּא וּמְרִירָא עַד לַחֲדָא
e: When Eisov heard his father’s words,
he wailed a most loud and bitter cry,
and he said to his father,
Bless me too, my father.
[Yitzchok] said, Your brother came with cunning [wisdom]
and he took [received] your blessing.

h: וַיֹּ֡אמֶר הֲכִי֩ קָרָ֨א שְׁמ֜וֹ יַעֲקֹ֗ב וַֽיַּעְקְבֵ֙נִי֙ זֶ֣ה פַעֲמַ֔יִם
t: וַאֲמַר יָאוּת קְרָא שְׁמֵיהּ יַעֲקֹב וְחַכְּמַנִי דְּנָן תַּרְתֵּין זִמְנִין
e: [Eisov] said, Is he not rightly called Yaakov? [He is rightly called Yaakov] He has deceived me twice;
he took my birthright,
and now he has taken [received] my blessing.
He said, Have you not saved a blessing for me?

h: וַיַּ֨עַן יִצְחָ֜ק וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לְעֵשָׂ֗ו הֵ֣ן גְּבִ֞יר שַׂמְתִּ֥יו לָךְ֙ וְאֶת־כָּל־אֶחָ֗יו נָתַ֤תִּי לוֹ֙ לַעֲבָדִ֔ים
t: וַאֲתֵיב יִצְחָק וַאֲמַר לְעֵשָׂו הָא רַב שַׁוִּתֵּיהּ לָךְ (<small>נ"א</small> עִלַּוָךְ) וְיָת כָּל אֲחוֹהִי יְהָבִית לֵיהּ לְעַבְדִּין
e: Yitzchok replied and said to Eisov. Behold, I have made him your master, and all his brothers I have given him as slaves.
I have sustained him with grain and wine.
Where? [Here.]
What can I do for you, my son?

h: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר עֵשָׂ֜ו אֶל־אָבִ֗יו הַֽבְרָכָ֨ה אַחַ֤ת הִֽוא־לְךָ֙ אָבִ֔י
t: וַאֲמַר עֵשָׂו לַאֲבוּהִי הֲבִרְכְּתָא חֲדָא הִיא לָךְ אַבָּא
e: Eisov said to his father, Do you have only one blessing, my father?
Bless me too, my father,
and Eisov raised his voice and wept.
Yitzchok, his father replied and said to him,
Behold the fatness [richness] [goodness] of the earth shall be your dwelling,
and of the dew of heaven from above.

t: וִיהֵי כַּד יַעְבְּרוּן בְּנוֹהִי עַל פִּתְגָּמֵי אוֹרַיְתָא
e: You shall live by your sword,
and you shall serve your brother.
When you have cause to be grieved [When his sons will transgress the words of the Torah],
you will throw off his yoke from your neck.

h: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר עֵשָׂ֜ו בְּלִבּ֗וֹ יִקְרְבוּ֙ יְמֵי֙ אֵ֣בֶל אָבִ֔י
t: וַאֲמַר עֵשָׂו בְּלִבֵּיהּ יִקְרְבוּן יוֹמֵי אֶבְלֵי דְאַבָּא
e: Eisov hated Yaakov
because of the blessing with which his father blessed him,
and Eisov said in his heart, The mourning days for my father are approaching.
I will then kill my brother, Yaakov.
Rivkah was informed
about the words of Eisov, her older son,
and she sent [a messenger] to call Yaakov, her younger son,
and she said to him.
Behold, your brother Eisov
is consoled through you [lying in wait for you], [for he intends] to kill you.

t: וְקוּם אִזֵיל לָךְ לְוַת לָבָן אָחִי לְחָרָן:
e: Now my son listen to [accept] me.
Get up and flee to Lavan, my brother, to Charan.
Remain with him a short time
until your brother’s fury has subsided.

h: עַד־שׁ֨וּב אַף־אָחִ֜יךָ מִמְּךָ֗ וְשָׁכַח֙ אֵ֣ת אֲשֶׁר־עָשִׂ֣יתָ לּ֔וֹ
t: עַד דִּיתוּב רוּגְזָא דְאָחוּךְ מִנָּךְ וְיִתְנְשֵׁי יָת דִּי עֲבַדְתָּ לֵיהּ
לְמָה אֶתְכַּל אַף תַּרְוֵיכוֹן יוֹמָא חָד:
e: Until your brother’s rage toward you has subsided, and he has forgotten what you did to him.
I will then send [for you] and bring you [back] from there.
Why should I lose both of you on one day?

h: אִם־לֹקֵ֣חַ יַ֠עֲקֹב אִשָּׁ֨ה מִבְּנֽוֹת־חֵ֤ת כָּאֵ֙לֶּה֙ מִבְּנ֣וֹת הָאָ֔רֶץ
t: אִם נְסִיב יַעֲקֹב אִתְּתָא מִבְּנַת חִתָּאָה כְאִלֵּין מִבְּנַת אַרְעָא
e: Rivkah said to Yitzchok,
I am disgusted with my life
because of the daughters of Cheis.
If Yaakov marries a woman of the daughters of Cheis, like these, from the daughters of the land,
what is life [worth] to me.
Yitzchok called Yaakov and blessed him.
He commanded him and said to him,
Do not marry a woman of the daughters of Canaan.

h: וְקַח־לְךָ֤ מִשָּׁם֙ אִשָּׁ֔ה מִבְּנ֥וֹת לָבָ֖ן אֲחִ֥י אִמֶּֽךָ׃
t: וְסַב לָךְ מִתַּמָּן אִתְּתָא מִבְּנַת לָבָן אֲחוּהָא דְאִמָּךְ:
e: Set out and go to Padan Aram,
to the house of Besueil, your mother’s father,
and marry one of the daughters of Lavan, your mother’s brother.
May the Almighty, Shaddai, bless you,
make you fruitful and multiply you.
May you become an assembly of peoples [tribes].
May He give you the blessing of Avraham,
to you and to your descendants with you,
that you may inherit the land of your dwelling
which God gave to Avraham.
Yitzchok sent Yaakov on his way,
and he went to Paddan Aram,
to Lavan, son of Besueil the Aramean,
the brother of Rivkah,
mother of Yaakov and Eisov.

t: וַחֲזָא עֵשָׂו אֲרֵי בָרִיךְ יִצְחָק יָת יַעֲקֹב
e: Eisov saw that Yitzchok blessed Yaakov,
and sent him to Paddan Aram,
to find a wife there;
and as he blessed him,
he commanded him saying,
Do not take a wife from the daughters of Canaan.
And Yaakov listened to [accepted]
his father and mother,
and went to Paddan Aram.
Eisov [thus] realized
that the daughters of Canaan were evil
in the eyes of Yitzchok, his father.

h: וַיִּקַּ֡ח אֶֽת־מָחֲלַ֣ת בַּת־יִשְׁמָעֵ֨אל בֶּן־אַבְרָהָ֜ם אֲח֧וֹת נְבָי֛וֹת עַל־נָשָׁ֖יו ל֥וֹ לְאִשָּֽׁה׃
t: וּנְסִיב יָת מַחֲלַת בַּת יִשְׁמָעֵאל בַּר אַבְרָהָם אֲחָתֵיהּ דִּנְבָיוֹת עַל נְשׁוֹהִי לֵיהּ לְאִנְתּוּ:
e: Eisov [then] went to Yishmael,
and took Mochalas, the daughter of Yishmael, the son of Avraham and sister of Nevayos, in addition to his other wives, for a wife.
